evidence: Fields `private readonly users = new Map<string, User>()`, `projects = new Map<string, Project>()` and `tasks = new Map<string, Task>()` act as in-memory storage (infrastructure/repository role)
Counters `nextUserId`, `nextProjectId` and `nextTaskId`, used as `String(this.nextTaskId++)` in createTask, generate IDs for storage (infrastructure role)
Private methods `getUser`, `getProject` and `getTask` read directly from those Maps (repository lookups belong to infrastructure)
markTaskDone: `if (task.status === "done") throw new DomainError("Task is already done", 409)` is a status-transition rule for the entity (domain role)
requireStatus and validateDueDate check entity values (domain role)
`new DomainError("User not found", 404)` and the 409 above put HTTP status codes in the application layer (transport/infrastructure role)
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
An application service should coordinate use cases. It should pass storage to repositories in infrastructure and leave entity rules to the domain. TaskManagementService does three jobs that belong to other layers:
1. Persistence (infrastructure): it stores users, projects and tasks in its own private Maps, creates IDs from counters, and looks records up directly. This is repository work with nothing between it and the use cases.
2. Entity rules (domain): checks such as "a task that is already done can't be marked done", the allowed status values, required title and description, and valid due dates are entity invariants. They are coded as private service methods instead of on the domain entities.
3. Transport details (infrastructure): it passes HTTP status codes (404, 409) when it throws errors, which ties the use cases to HTTP.
The persistence job alone is enough to fail the rule.

violations.message: TaskManagementService handles persistence itself: the private Maps `users`, `projects` and `tasks`, the ID counters `nextUserId`, `nextProjectId` and `nextTaskId`, and the Map lookups in getUser, getProject and getTask. This is repository work that belongs in the infrastructure layer.
Entity rules sit in the application service instead of the domain: markTaskDone's 'already done' check, requireStatus, validateDueDate, and requireText for title and description.
HTTP status codes (404 in getUser, getProject and getTask; 409 in markTaskDone) are passed to DomainError, which puts a transport concern in the application layer.
